feedback: has_matching_key reads is_locked on the door after unlock; Door.toggle clears is_locked when unlocking, so once the agent has unlocked the door (and thus plausibly has the key, or the door is later closed while the key is held) the color L cannot be recovered from is_locked — per the code notes, the locked door's color/cell must be captured at the first labeling step and reused. This predicate therefore fails after unlocking even when the agent correctly carries the matching key. target_door_open has the same flaw: it searches for a door with is_locked true and is_open true, but unlocking clears is_locked, so target_door_open is never true — the reward machine can never progress past u2. target_room_entered also depends on cell.is_locked (and its '(cell.is_open or True)' is a no-op that does not fix it): the locked-door cell cannot be found by is_locked after unlocking, so the room-entry test breaks after the door is opened. key_found and target_picked_up are correct. Fix by identifying the locked door once (its color and position) at the first step and reusing that color/position across all propositions, per the documented caution.

`has_matching_key` should simply check `env.carrying.type == "key" and env.carrying.color == L`; the extra door-scan conditions make it wrong: it fails once the key is carried but the door has been unlocked (then `is_locked` is False and the guard requires `is_open or is_locked`, which fails if the door was later shut), and it can be true even if the agent picked up some other color key coinciding with an unlocked door color (e.g. after unlocking the door with the wrong key). `target_door_open` must be the openness of the *locked* door regardless of what the agent carries; requiring the agent to hold the matching key makes it wrongly false after the agent drops the key, though the spec says it can be toggled shut but should track the locked door's `is_open` (the code notes lock the door's color/cell at first labeling). `target_room_entered` must latch on the fixed locked-door cell and be true whenever the agent stands in that room's 6x6 block; tying it to carrying the matching key and an open door misfires (e.g. false after dropping the key while inside the room) and tests the wrong room when multiple doors share the color. None of these three predicates may depend on `env.carrying`; they must identify the locked door once at episode start and reuse its stored color/cell.
